title: The paddle steamer
standfirst: A few historic paddle steamers still sail the Nile, restored in the style of the early twentieth century. This is one of the vessel types in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: What a Nile paddle steamer is
paragraphs: Paddle steamers were the river’s passenger ships before modern cruise ships. The few that remain have been restored, with period cabins, wood and brass, and a slow, steady pace. They are larger than a dahabiya and much smaller than most cruise ships.

sections.heading: Life on board
paragraphs: Expect fewer guests than on a cruise ship, a quieter atmosphere and a sense of history. Facilities are fewer: there may be no pool. Routes are usually the classic Luxor to Aswan sailing.

sections.heading: Is a paddle steamer for you?
paragraphs: Choose a steamer if the character of the boat matters to you as much as the sights. There are very few, so they book up early in the cooler months.

faqs.q: How many paddle steamers sail the Nile?
faqs.a: Only a handful. Our vessel directory lists three.
They keep a gentler pace than motor ships, but follow similar routes and stops.
